answer: An attester must stake 24% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. Because the ridge stake is held until the karst settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the island audit lists each exposure. A farm running 124 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. That is 40 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
